MESSAGE:
Hi! I'm organising a half-day community workshop at the library on a Saturday and I'm drowning in logistics.

First, a title for the event. It's about helping small local groups get better at social media, so something friendly.

The room is ours from 09:00 to 14:00, hard stop. Sessions: a 60-minute keynote, a 45-minute panel, a 90-minute hands-on workshop, 30 minutes of lightning talks, and a 45-minute lunch. The keynote speaker can't arrive before 10:00. The panel moderator has to leave by 11:00, so the panel needs to be finished by then. The caterers deliver at 12:15 and the food can't sit around, so lunch has to start between 12:15 and 12:45. The workshop has to come before lunch, and after it we need 15 minutes to reset the room before whatever comes next. Could you lay out a full timetable that works?

Could you also write a two-sentence blurb for the library newsletter? And what's a good colour for the name badges? We're printing on white card. Recommend whether to do registration with a paper sign-up sheet or an online form for a mostly older crowd, and give me three icebreaker ideas that don't involve anyone standing up and talking about themselves. Oh, and one more: could you draft a short thank-you email we can send to attendees afterwards, with a link to a feedback form? Two or three sentences is plenty.

REQUESTS:
1. Suggest a friendly event title
2. Lay out a full timetable satisfying all room, speaker, catering and reset constraints  KEY: Any timetable that satisfies ALL: within 09:00-14:00; panel (45) ends by 11:00; keynote (60) starts at or after 10:00; workshop (90) before lunch followed by a 15-min reset; lunch (45) starts 12:15-12:45; lightning talks (30) fit. Only 15 min of slack overall. Valid example: Panel 09:00-09:45, Keynote 10:00-11:00, Workshop 11:00-12:30, reset 12:30-12:45, Lunch 12:45-13:30, Lightning 13:30-14:00. Another: Panel 09:00-09:45, Workshop 09:45-11:15, reset, Keynote 11:30-12:30, Lunch 12:30-13:15, Lightning 13:15-13:45. Scorer: check each constraint; any violation = incorrect.
3. Write a two-sentence newsletter blurb
4. Suggest a name-badge colour
5. Recommend paper sign-up vs online form for registration
6. Give three icebreakers that avoid self-introductions
7. Draft a short post-event thank-you email with a feedback link

ANSWER:
# Community Workshop Plan

## Title
**"Social Made Simple: A Friendly Workshop for Local Groups"**

Alternatives: *"Post, Share, Connect: Social Media for Community Groups"* or *"Getting Social: Helping Local Groups Shine Online."*

## Timetable

| Time | Session |
|---|---|
| 09:00–09:15 | Arrival, registration & coffee |
| 09:15–10:00 | Panel (45 min) |
| 10:00–10:30 | Lightning talks (30 min) |
| 10:30–12:00 | Hands-on workshop (90 min) |
| 12:00–12:15 | Room reset (15 min) |
| 12:15–13:00 | Lunch (45 min) |
| 13:00–14:00 | Keynote (60 min) |

**How each constraint is met:**
- **Panel:** It ends at 10:00, an hour before the moderator has to leave.
- **Keynote:** It starts at 13:00, so the speaker has three hours of leeway after their 10:00 arrival.
- **Workshop and reset:** The workshop comes before lunch, and the 15-minute reset follows it.
- **Lunch:** It starts at 12:15, which is inside the 12:15–12:45 window.
- **Hard stop:** Everything finishes at 14:00, and the 15 spare minutes become a welcome slot at 09:00.

**Watch-outs:**
- Lunch starts the moment the food arrives. Ask the caterers to come a few minutes early or to set up while the room is being reset.
- The keynote runs right up to the hard stop. Brief the speaker to finish on time, and have volunteers start packing up quietly at 13:50.

**Alternative:** Run the panel 09:15–10:00, keynote 10:00–11:00, workshop 11:00–12:30, reset 12:30–12:45, lunch 12:45–13:30 and lightning talks 13:30–14:00. This gives the caterers a 30-minute buffer and ends on the easily trimmed lightning talks. The downside is that the keynote speaker must start the moment they arrive.

## Newsletter Blurb
Join us at the library on Saturday for *Social Made Simple*, a friendly half-day workshop for clubs, charities and community groups who want to get more from social media. With a keynote, a panel, lightning talks, hands-on practice and lunch included, you'll leave with practical ideas you can use straight away.

## Badge Colour
Use **deep teal or navy** for the names and a colour band. On white card, both are easy to read for older eyes and look calm and professional. Print names large (at least 24pt) in a plain font. Avoid pale colours like yellow, light green or pastels, since they fade into the white.

## Registration
I recommend a **paper sign-up sheet** at the library desk, with a phone number for people who prefer to call. Most older attendees will find this the most comfortable option. If you want an online form too, keep it as a secondary option, and use one master list so you don't count anyone twice.

## Icebreakers (no standing up and talking about yourself)
1. **Post-it map:** Put a big local map on the wall and have people stick a note where their group meets.
2. **Table challenge:** Each table writes down the best social media post they've seen from a local group, and the room votes on a favourite.
3. **"Find someone who…" bingo:** A card with squares like "has posted on Facebook this week" or "runs a group with over 50 members." People mingle and collect initials, with no speeches needed.

## Thank-You Email
**Subject:** Thank you for joining Social Made Simple!

Thank you so much for coming to Social Made Simple at the library on Saturday. It was wonderful to see so many local groups sharing ideas. We'd love to hear what you thought, so please take two minutes to fill in our feedback form: [LINK]

Warm wishes,
[Your name]
